patch.value: Reconcile duplicate-event semantics between the identical-blob shortcut and the append-only history union

mergeTrees keeps one copy when both sides changed a history blob to the same id (git's identical-blob rule), while mergeAppendOnlyLog (since the PR #91 review fix for 4183822298) keeps one occurrence per side, so a byte-identical event appended on both sides survives twice when the sides differ elsewhere. The outcome therefore depends on unrelated edits. Byte-identical pm events (same ms timestamp, author, op, patch) on two branches realistically come from a cherry-pick or the same commit merged into both, where duplication would replay one event twice. Decide one rule (likely: dedupe byte-identical appended events) and apply it in both paths, validated against the pm CLI's own pm-history merge driver on real (hash-chain-valid) events.

Same-input merges give the same history whether or not the two blobs are identical; the chosen rule is checked against pm's pm-history driver on real pm-written events; tests cover cherry-picked events and genuinely distinct events with equal content

Event identity is the byte-exact JSONL line. For a shared base and two sides: (1) an event present in the base appears exactly once; (2) an event appended on only one side appears exactly once; (3) a byte-identical event appended on both sides appears exactly once (cherry-pick or the same commit merged into both), whether or not the two blobs are otherwise identical; (4) distinct appended events from both sides all appear, base kept as a strict prefix. The identical-blob shortcut and mergeAppendOnlyLog produce the same result for every case. The rule is checked against the pm CLI's pm-history merge driver on hash-chain-valid pm-written events, and tests cover cases 1-4.

Event identity is the byte-exact JSONL line; results are a multiset union over a shared base. (1) Base occurrences are kept exactly, including repeated identical lines, and the base stays a strict prefix. (2) Lines appended on only one side keep that side's multiplicity, so two identical appends on one side stay two (as test/review-findings.test.ts expects). (3) A line appended on both sides appears max(countA, countB) times, so a cherry-picked or doubly merged event appears once, not twice, whether or not the two blobs are otherwise identical. (4) Distinct appended events from both sides all appear. The identical-blob shortcut and mergeAppendOnlyLog produce the same result in every case; the rule is checked against the pm CLI's pm-history merge driver on hash-chain-valid pm-written events, and tests cover cases 1-4 including repeated lines in the base and on one side.
